answered.sql: SELECT initiative_name, description FROM Initiatives WHERE id IN (SELECT initiative_id FROM Community_Development_Corporations_Initiatives GROUP BY initiative_id HAVING COUNT(community_development_corporation_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Community_Development_Corporations)) ORDER BY initiative_name

candidates.meaning: For each CDC, list all initiatives associated with it.
candidates.sql: SELECT CDC.name, I.initiative_name FROM Community_Development_Corporations CDC JOIN Community_Development_Corporations_Initiatives CCI ON CDC.id = CCI.community_development_corporation_id JOIN Initiatives I ON CCI.initiative_id = I.id

candidates.meaning: List all initiatives associated with each community development corporation.
candidates.sql: SELECT cdc.name, i.initiative_name FROM Community_Development_Corporations cdc JOIN Community_Development_Corporations_Initiatives cdc_init ON cdc.id = cdc_init.community_development_corporation_id JOIN Initiatives i ON cdc_init.initiative_id = i.id

candidates.meaning: Count the number of initiatives for each community development corporation.
candidates.sql: SELECT cdc.name, COUNT(cdc_init.initiative_id) AS initiative_count FROM Community_Development_Corporations cdc JOIN Community_Development_Corporations_Initiatives cdc_init ON cdc.id = cdc_init.community_development_corporation_id GROUP BY cdc.name

candidates.meaning: Identify the most common initiative across all community development corporations.
candidates.sql: SELECT i.initiative_name, COUNT(cdc_init.initiative_id) AS initiative_count FROM Initiatives i JOIN Community_Development_Corporations_Initiatives cdc_init ON i.id = cdc_init.initiative_id GROUP BY i.initiative_name ORDER BY initiative_count DESC LIMIT 1
